knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The handover records observed and authorised work, lists unresolved conditions and named referrals, and claims no safety certification. The other options are a certification claim, an unrecorded verbal summary, or a record with no open conditions.
The statement is not supported by ground-level observation, so it is declined in writing with the reason. The observed scope, the limits and a specialist referral are recorded.

Under the consumer rules, extra work needs the customer's permission before it is done, and the agreement is recorded. Starting first and billing later, or acting on a verbal instruction alone, are both wrong.

practicalCriteria: Compares a mock work order with a mock observation record, and separates completed scope from excluded elevations.
Writes a restricted handover with completed scope, excluded elevations, unresolved conditions and named referrals, and with a limits statement.
Declines a simulated request for an all-windows-certified-safe statement in writing, with the reason and a referral.
Refers a simulated extra-scope request to the supervisor, and records the written agreement required before any work.
passRule: Restricted handover complete with no unsupported claim, unsupported certificate declined in writing, and extra scope held until written agreement is recorded. Observed on paper or in a supervised tabletop exercise. A knowledge check result alone is not a pass.
evidenceRequired: Restricted handover with the four sections and limits statement
Written decline for the simulated certificate request
Scope change record showing written agreement or refusal
stopWorkCriteria: Recommends unapproved access or work at height
Assumes site permission, equipment clearance or competence without checking it
Signs or issues a certificate or statement of safety without authority
Starts extra scope before written agreement is recorded
